newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Vietnamese envoy in Morocco to restore ties.
newsitem.headline: Vietnamese envoy in Morocco to restore ties.

text.p: Vietnamese Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam began a 24-hour visit on Monday intended to restore diplomatic ties with Rabat, suspended for nearly two decades over the Western Sahara dispute, an official source said.
"It is the first visit of a Vietnamese official delegation to Rabat since the Western Sahara conflict erupted in 1976," the source said.
The official MAP news agency said the Vietnamese minister held "constructive talks" with government officials in Rabat.
"The time has come for Morocco and Vietnam to promote cooperation and trade," MAP quoted Trade Minister Driss Jettou as saying after a meeting with the Vietnamese delegation.
Rabat and Hanoi are expected to examine the possibility of signing a trade, cooperation and investment agreement, MAP said, but gave no other details.
Relations deteriorated after 1976 when Vietnam strongly supported the Algeria-backed Polisario Front.
Polisario guerrillas and Moroccan troops fought for control of the Western Sahara for more than 17 years until a 1991 U.N.-sponsored truce.
A U.N. referendum to decide the future of the former Spanish colony was originally due in 1992 but has been stalled by arguments over who is eligible to take part in the vote.
